Documentation

Layering System

Semantic z-index management with the z() function. Build predictable stacking contexts.

Interactive Demo

Click the buttons to toggle layers and visualize the stacking order. Layers higher in the stack appear in front of lower layers.

guides z("guides") z-index: 9998
modal z("modal") z-index: 7000
interface z("interface") z-index: 4000
content z("content") z-index: 2000
canvas z("canvas") z-index: -1000

Stack Order

Visual representation of the layer stack. Elements are ordered from bottom (canvas) to top (guides). Higher z-index values appear in front.

canvas z-index: -1000
content z-index: 2000
interface z-index: 4000
modal z-index: 7000
guides z-index: 9998

Use Cases

Each layer is designed for specific UI patterns:

guides
Development Overlays

Grid guides, alignment helpers, debug overlays, measurement tools

modal
Modal Dialogs

Lightboxes, confirmations, image galleries, video players

interface
Fixed UI

Sticky headers, navigation bars, toolbars, floating buttons

content
Main Content

Cards, dropdowns, tooltips, popovers, image overlays

canvas
Background

Page backgrounds, decorative elements, ambient animations

Layer Reference

Layer Function z-index Description
guides z("guides") 9998 Development guides and debug overlays
modal z("modal") 7000 Modal dialogs, lightboxes, popups
interface z("interface") 4000 Fixed navigation, sticky elements
content z("content") 2000 Main content with elevation
canvas z("canvas") -1000 Background layer elements

Usage

// Import the layer function @use "unit.gl" as *; // Use semantic layer names instead of magic numbers .modal-overlay { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: z("modal"); // 7000 } .sticky-header { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: z("interface"); // 4000 } .card { position: relative; z-index: z("content"); // 2000 } .background-pattern { position: absolute; z-index: z("canvas"); // -1000 } // Use offsets for related elements .dropdown-trigger { z-index: z("content"); // 2000 } .dropdown-menu { z-index: z("content") + 10; // 2010 } .modal-backdrop { z-index: z("modal") - 1; // 6999 }

Customization

You can extend or modify the default layer map:

// Add custom layers to $layer_map $layer_map: ( "canvas": -1000, "background": 0, "content": 2000, "dropdown": 3000, // Custom layer "sticky": 3500, // Custom layer "interface": 4000, "overlay": 5000, // Custom layer "modal": 7000, "toast": 8000, // Custom layer "tooltip": 8500, // Custom layer "guides": 9998, ) !default; // Then use your custom layers .toast-notification { z-index: z("toast"); // 8000 }

Best Practices

Tip

Use semantic layer names consistently across your project to avoid z-index conflicts and maintain predictable stacking behavior.

  • Never use arbitrary z-index values — Always use the z() function with semantic names
  • Use offsets for related elements — Add +1, +10 for elements that should stack relative to a layer
  • Keep the gap between layers — The default 1000-2000 gaps allow plenty of room for offsets
  • Document custom layers — If you add layers to $layer_map, document their purpose
  • Consider stacking contexts — Remember that position: fixed/absolute with z-index creates new stacking contexts
